copies.standard:
Where do hams actually talk, trade, and help each other out? A lot of it happens on local swap nets.

I keep a free directory of swap nets on HamRadioBargains.com: nets across the country, listed by day and time, so you can find one near you and check in. New hams use it to meet people locally. Old hands use it to hear what is for sale before it ever hits a listing.

The directory is here: https://hamradiobargains.com/on-the-air/swap-nets/

Know a net that should be listed? There is a form on that page. Send it in and I will add it.

73, Leo K4LFC
copies.standard_alt:
Quick one for the group: I keep a free monthly calendar of what is on the air, contests, QSO parties, and special events, written in plain English.

It is called On the Air, on HamRadioBargains.com. Each month it explains what is coming up, when the bands will be busy, and what each event is like to join. Handy if you are planning your weekends around the radio.

See this month here: https://hamradiobargains.com/on-the-air/

73, Leo K4LFC
copies.dx_full:
Hello all — 40+ years a ham, and a regular reader here.

Quick heads-up on a free page I keep that this group may get some use out of in November: it's called On the Air, on HamRadioBargains.com. Every month it writes up the DX contests and QSO parties in plain English — what the contest is, when the bands will be busy, and what it's like to jump in — no rulebook-speak. November is a strong month: Sweepstakes CW next weekend (Nov 7–9), Sweepstakes on phone two weeks later (Nov 21–23), and the month closes with CQ WW on CW (Nov 28–29) — October was voice, November ends in code.

The same site also tracks what used gear actually sells for, from recorded sales, and posts listings priced around 25% below that fair value — plus a free price checker if you're valuing a rig to buy or sell. But honestly, the On the Air page is the part I built for groups like this one.

Hope it's useful. See you in the pileups. 73
